assertions.interpretation: The scene is set at the time when Ruan Xuanzi is discussing whether ghosts and spirits exist.
Some people hold the view that when a person dies, a ghost remains — this is the prevailing opinion being discussed at the time.

assertions.exact_span: 今見鬼者云箸生時衣服
assertions.interpretation: At the present time, those who claim to see ghosts say the ghosts wear the clothes they wore while alive — this is the immediate claim being refuted.

assertions.interpretation: The Lunheng (論衡) is quoted as a precedent asserting that the world's claim that the dead become ghosts is wrong.
Continuation of the Lunheng quotation: the dead do not become ghosts; there is no ghost.

assertions.exact_span: 由此言之見衣服象人則形體亦象人
assertions.interpretation: The annotation reasons from the Lunheng argument: if clothes resemble a person, then the body also resembles a person — an inferential step in the cited argument.

assertions.interpretation: If it resembles a person, one knows it is not a dead person — continuation of the cited argument.

assertions.exact_span: 從裸袒之形無爲見衣帶被服也
assertions.interpretation: From the naked form, there is no reason to see clothing and belts — further cited reasoning about why ghosts cannot wear clothes.

assertions.interpretation: Why? Because clothes have no spirit — the cited argument's conclusion about clothes lacking spiritual substance.
